chapter: Ella, Charlie Christian and Europe with Hayes
title: Charlie Christian at Minton's, and his final illness
summary: Late in 1941 Clarke met Charlie Christian, who came to Minton's with Mike Bryan and left his amp there; a nurse friend cared for Charlie at the hospital until he died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, and when I went back to Minton's that's when I met Charlie Christian.
Well, how much longer did Charlie have to go there? Not very much longer, did he?
No. Charlie died before I -- he died in 1942.
He and Mike Bryan used to come up. I lived on the hill, you know?
At the Douglas Hotel, and we had a -- it was a nice park, a nice green park up there.
And Mike Bryan used to bring Charlie up.
The guitar player who was with Benny
They had Mike was playing rhythm and Charlie was playing solos.
And Mike used to bring Charlie up and we would all lay on the grass and talk, you know. And well, Minton's --
So Charlie was digging what you were doing.
Yeah, he'd come every chance he got. He was there. In fact he left his speaker there.
So all he had to do was bring his guitar and plug in and start playing.
Yeah, he dug right away what was going on.
He'd have -- he'd have gone -- you know, he'd have broken more ground all the time I guess, wouldn't he?
Oh, yes. We were supposed to form a group you know.
That was what was heartbreaking when -- and Big Sid had been out to the hospital to see Charlie.

And he told him a joke or something, and Charlie laughed so hard that he had a coughing spell. And a nurse who was a very good friend of mine -- and I told her -- I knew she was working there, it was the Seaview, I think it was.
Well, she was kind of a nurse of authority, you know.

And I said to her, I said, 'Listen, there's a very dear friend of mine in your hospital whose name is Charlie Christian, and I wish you would take care of him.' So you know, she took care of him until he died, right at his bedside. That's how faithful she was. And she loved Charlie. When Charlie used to take his guitar out and play, you know, the doctor would say, 'Charlie, don't play your guitar. You can't play your guitar.' And she would say, 'Oh, let him play,' you know. She knew he wasn't going to live long anyway, so -- and --
That was a real sad thing, wasn't it?
